questions.emi_instruction: For each of the description below, identify the psychoanalytical concept from the list below
questions.question_text:
This refers to any hindrance noted in the course of therapeutic progress during
psychotherapy
questions.explanation:
1) Transference refers to a displacement of feelings and attitudes derived from past relationships and experiences onto the therapist. It is
bidimensional - includes replaying past experiences + seeking a new relationship with the therapist. It may involve idealizing, erotic or highly
negative and denigrating approaches. Countertransference can be regarded as the transference from an analyst on to the patient due to the
past experiences of the analyst. Initially viewed as a resistance or obstacle to therapy, this is now regarded to be due to both analysts' past
experiences and also the reaction of an analyst to what the patient projects onto him/her. Hence analyzing countertransference can provide
insight into a patient's psychic state in the same sense as analyzing transference.

questions.emi_instruction: Match each of the proponents below with their therapy/school listed below
questions.question_text: Jacob Moreno
questions.explanation:
Carl Rogers is best known for his contributions to a humanistic form of therapy initially called as non-directive therapy. He felt that the client
should direct the progress of the therapy. The therapist should not lead the client, but rather be there for the client. It is also known as client
centred or Rogerian therapy.  
Jacob Levy Moreno, the originator of psychodrama, was a Viennese doctor who practiced with storytelling in children's groups, and it is
followed by having the children act out the stories. He later used this method with adults that formed the basis for psychodrama.  
Moreno entered psychodrama through the practice of sociometry. It is an observational charting of how people interact in groups.
